exposure: Clinical manifestations (e.g., motor features, dysmorphic features, oculogyric movements, autonomic dysfunction, acquired microcephaly)
Molecular genetic findings (e.g., specific genes like SPG, HPRT1, TH, QDPR, DDC, ADCY5, NIKX2-1, CANA1A, PDHA1, AT, SLC2A1, SPR)
outcome: Delineation of clinical manifestations and molecular findings in CP mimic patients
Identification of specific genetic causes for CP mimics
Potential for specific disease-modifying therapy and genetic counseling
cohort: The study included 47 patients diagnosed with Cerebral Palsy (CP) but without an acquired etiology, characterized as CP mimics, from a Greek tertiary care center.
finding: Specific genetic causes for CP mimics were identified in 23 out of 47 patients, leading to etiological diagnoses and, in some cases, specific treatments, with CP mimics presenting distinct clinical features from classic CP.
